general_information.Syllabus Name: Multimedia Production Project_Dự án sản xuất sản phẩm TTĐPT
general_information.Description: This course will describe five primary stages in a multimedia project and determine the scope of a multimedia project. These may include phases, tasks, costs, timelines, and elements of a multimedia project proposal. Students will learn how to apply artificial intelligence (AI) tools and digital technologies to enhance project performance. They will use these tools to optimize content creation, streamline workflows, and improve project management across multimedia projects. In addition, this course gives students opportunities to practice working on a real-life project. The lecturer will use several teaching methods, such as conducting group discussions and sharing fieldwork experience, in addition to regular teaching. Students will have the chance to present their work as well as their thinking process related to the project.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Attend at least 80% of class hours to be accepted for the final examination. - Actively participate in class activities. - Fulfill tasks given by the instructor after class. - Use their own laptop in class only for learning purposes. - Read the textbook in advance - Access the course website (www.cms.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information, course materials, online support from teachers and other students, and for practices and assessments.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Explain the five main stages of a multimedia project, the intangible factors affecting production quality, the key team roles with their required skills, and the common hardware/software tools used. Includes guidance on selecting suitable platforms for effective multimedia production.
Analyze and determine the scope, objectives, target audience, creative strategy, and budget of a multimedia project, examine the intangible elements needed to make good multimedia production

Develop a complete project plan with clear phases, tasks, schedules, resource allocation, and a well-defined project scope. Evaluate project requirements such as cost, timeline, workload, and risks necessary for completing a multimedia project.
Apply multimedia production tools and AI-based tools to optimize workflows and enhance project efficiency.
Evaluate overall quality of the project, delivers the intended message or experience, and fulfills user needs within the defined scope and constraints.

Have accountability, good self-organization, and strong collaborative skills while working with the team on the multimedia project. Contribute actively and communicates effectively to support overall project success.

assessments.Note: Participation grades will be given based on students' preparation, quality of participation, and group performance.

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Test the acquired knowledge which students obtained in the delivered chapters (Chapters 7, 8, 9, 11, 14).
assessments.Grading Guide: Weight: 50% Components: Presentation (20%) + Report (30%) - Task Description: This assessment includes one group report and one group presentation. It provides students with an opportunity to understand their product and the production process by working on a real-life project. Students are recommended to use AI tools to support idea generation and planning. By taking on roles such as director, producer, marketer, etc., this project helps students develop ideas and conduct research related to cost, timeline, target audience, and other elements across different types of multimedia products. Students are also expected to provide visual content and select appropriate media channels to convey their intended message to the target audience. Students will work in groups of 3 or 4 to complete this project. AI tools may be used to enhance workflow efficiency and overall project performance. - Presentation (20%): For the 30-minute presentation, students are required to present the key points from their report to help classmates gain insights into various roles in the production process and understand the challenges associated with each role. The presentation must clearly demonstrate the project plan, including: the production timeline, estimated billing rates, strategies to reach the target audience, and the media platforms chosen to deliver the intended message. - Report (30%: Title of the report Provide an overview of the group project selected during the 10 weeks and explain the rationale for choosing a particular product type (e.g., Website, TVC, Short Film, etc.). The report must present the five stages of the production process: ideas, pre-production, production, post-production, and distribution Observation and Interactions: Explain each stage and describe how and where the research and information were obtained. Reflection: Reflect on your experience working with your teammates, as well as on your production process and your target audience. Discuss key lessons learned throughout the project. Notes: Detailed marking criteria for this assessment will be provided by your lecturer.

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Test the acquired knowledge which students obtained in the delivered chapters (Chapters 7 and 8).
assessments.Grading Guide: Type: Essay Weight: 30% Components: Presentation (10%) + Essay (20%) Task Description: This assessment provides students with an opportunity to reflect deeply on their assigned role in the multimedia production process. Students are required to describe their role from an insider’s perspective and reflect on the timeline, responsibilities, interactions with teammates, and research undertaken. The task also allows students to identify key roles within the production process and determine which role(s) and characteristics best represent themselves as multimedia practitioners. Presentation (10%): For the 10-minute presentation, students must present the key points discussed in their essay. The presentation should help classmates gain insights into the role(s) you undertook, how you communicated and collaborated with your teammates, how you planned and executed your tasks, advantages and disadvantages associated with your role(s), and your understanding of the overall production process. Your presentation should clearly convey how you approached your responsibilities and how your role contributed to the team’s workflow. Essay (20%): Your reflective essay should illustrate who you are as a member of the production team. Reflecting on your own role will help you better understand yourself, your teammates, and the production workflow within the multimedia industry. Your reflective essay must include the following sections: - Title of your essay - Provide a brief description of the chosen product and identify your role and your teammates’ roles. Include the timeline required to complete your assigned tasks. - Reflect what you have learnt and identify as member of your group, how this role shapes your thinking and doing Notes: Detailed marking criteria for this assessment will be provided by your lecturer.
